key_insight: A backward-mapping, genome-guided pipeline can translate device targets into chemically interpretable rules to discover phase-stable, lead-free double perovskites.
engineering_relevance: The workflow offers a practical inverse-design route for scalable screening of halide perovskites with stability, optical, and transport properties aligned to photovoltaic and optoelectronic device needs.
method: Start with 13,088 charge-balanced A2BB'X6 compositions and apply halide-aware formability filtering.
Encode six families of chemical-genome descriptors and train evolutionary-optimized ML surrogates for stability and band gap.
Use SHAP interpretation plus DFT closure to validate and refine candidate materials.
evidence_signal: From the abstract, the funnel narrows 13,088 compositions to seven DFT-validated candidates, with stability labeled by Ehull and band gaps predicted for target-driven selection.
watch_item: Results rely on PBE-based surrogate targets and DFT validation, so experimental synthesis, phase purity, and temperature-dependent stability still need confirmation.
paper_title: Backward Mapping from Device Targets to Chemical Genomes for Interpretable Discovery of Phase-Stable Lead-Free Double Perovskites with DFT-Validated Design Rules
